title: 01. Foundations: What are Large Language Models (LLMs)?
summary: A language model is a system that understands and generates human language.

sections.title: 2.1 What is a Language Model?
sections.body:
### Start with the Basics
A **language model** is a system that understands and generates human language.

Think of **autocomplete on your phone** — when you type "I am going to the..." your phone suggests "store" or "gym." That's a tiny language model!

### What Makes it "LARGE"?
LLMs are trained on:
- **Massive amounts of text** — books, websites, Wikipedia, code, articles (trillions of words!)
- Using **billions or trillions of parameters** (like dials/settings that get tuned during training)

| Model | Parameters | Training Data |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| GPT-2 (2019) | 1.5 Billion | 40GB of text |
| GPT-3 (2020) | 175 Billion | 570GB of text |
| GPT-4 (2023) | ~1 Trillion | Unknown (huge!) |
| Llama 3 (2024) | 70-400 Billion | 15 Trillion tokens |

### The "Predict Next Word" Secret 🤫
> **LLMs are fundamentally trained to predict the next word (token) in a sequence.**

That's it. That's the core idea!

**Example:**
```
Input:  "The sky is ____"
LLM thinks: "I've seen millions of sentences. After 'The sky is', 
             the word 'blue' appears most often."
Output: "blue"
```

But because they're trained on SO much data, this simple task of "predict the next word" leads to emergent abilities like:
- Answering questions
- Writing code
- Translating languages
- Summarizing documents
- Reasoning through problems

### Analogy: The Super-Intern
> Imagine hiring an intern who has **read every book, article, website, and document ever written** before starting their job. They haven't "experienced" the world, but they've absorbed massive amounts of human knowledge through reading.

That's an LLM.
